title: Anthocyanin Accumulation and Transcriptional Changes Associated with a Transient Purple-Leaf Phenotype in Liriodendron chinense
content: Anthocyanins contribute to leaf pigmentation in many woody ornamental plants, but the metabolic and transcriptional changes accompanying transient purple coloration in Liriodendron chinense remain poorly understood. Here, a naturally occurring purple-leaf variant propagated by stem cuttings was characterized by measuring total anthocyanin content and combining targeted anthocyanin profiling with RNA sequencing and quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR). Total anthocyanin content peaked in developing purple leaves (1.92 mg g⁻¹ FW) and declined by over 90% in mature leaves that had turned green, approaching the level of normal green-leaf plants. Targeted metabolomics showed that several cyanidin derivatives, particularly cyanidin-3,5-O-diglucoside, cyanidin-3-O-glucoside, and cyanidin-3-O-rutinoside, were more abundant at the purple-leaf stages. Transcriptome analysis identified developmental differences in the expression of flavonoid- and anthocyanin-biosynthetic genes, as well as differential expression of several MYB and bHLH transcription factor genes. Among these candidates, LhMYB113 displayed an expression pattern associated with the purple-leaf phenotype, which was also observed by qRT-PCR. Together, these findings associate transient purple coloration in this L. chinense variant with developmental changes in cyanidin-derived anthocyanins and the expression of related biosynthetic and regulatory genes. LhMYB113 represents a candidate for further functional analysis.
